papers_read.title_as_printed: Biomarker Extraction Based on Subspace Learning for the Prediction of Mild Cognitive Impairment Conversion (Li et al., BioMed Res. Int. 2021)
Features of the superficial white matter as biomarkers for the detection of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment: A diffusion tensor imaging study (Bigham et al., Heliyon 2022)

what_each_reports.P-185: pMCI vs sMCI (3-year window) from baseline 1.5T cortical thickness and volume projected through a subspace learned on AD/NC; 221 ADNI MCI (126 pMCI, 95 sMCI); 20 x 10-fold CV; best Acc 69.37% (linear SVM), AUC 0.6951.
what_each_reports.P-152: Cross-sectional diagnostic classification from DTI features of the superficial white matter, ADNI2, 72 subjects (24 HC, 24 MCI, 24 AD), 5-fold CV. The 95.8% is AD vs HC (AUC 0.99); MCI vs HC 83.3% (AUC 0.88); AD vs MCI 83.3% (AUC 0.93). There is no MCI-conversion analysis.

quantity_a: Accuracy for MCI-to-AD conversion within 3 years (pMCI vs sMCI) from baseline structural MRI morphometry.
quantity_b: Accuracy for cross-sectional AD vs healthy-control diagnosis from diffusion MRI features.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable: P-152 reports no conversion result, so there is nothing to set against P-185's 69.37%.

gates.task: mismatch: T2 conversion (P-185) vs AD-vs-HC diagnosis (P-152; registry Task_Type T3). The record's 'Yes' is wrong.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: T1 cortical thickness/volume vs diffusion tensor imaging of superficial white matter.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: different comparison (pMCI vs sMCI vs AD vs HC) and different modality; only the metric name (accuracy) is shared.
performance_validity: flag applies to P-152 had this been a performance comparison: its AD-vs-HC result is AUC 0.99 (accuracy 95.8%) on 48 subjects with internal 5-fold CV and no external cohort.
independence: Distinct author groups and ADNI phases; no shared cohort evident.
grounds: The record's claim 'P-152: Acc 95.8 on T2' misreads P-152: the 95.8% separates AD from healthy controls, and the paper reports no conversion analysis.
With that misreading removed there is no disagreement: P-185 reports conversion prediction and P-152 reports cross-sectional diagnosis (task and modality gates both fail).
P-152's figure would in any case fall under the performance-validity exclusion (AUC 0.99, n=48, internal CV only).

evidence_quotes.quote: The pro-posed biomarker achieved highest accuracy of 69.37% when using SVM classiﬁer with linear kernel.
Moreover, the 221 MCI subjects contain 126 pMCI and 95 sMCI subjects.
The linear kernel of SVM was the best classiﬁer, with an accuracy of 95.8% between the AD and HC groups
This method employed DTI data from 72 subjects: 24 subjects as HC, 24 subjects with MCI, and 24 subjects with AD.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-152: Acc 95.8 on T2' is wrong: 95.8% is AD vs HC; P-152 has no T2 result.
task_equal 'Yes' is wrong (the registry itself codes P-152 as T3).
resolution_note's 'Task mismatch from summaries: T2_conversion vs T1_mci_vs_hc' misidentifies the cited figure, which is AD vs HC, not MCI vs HC.
modality_family_equal 'Yes' is wrong: DTI vs T1 morphometry.
The registry Sample_N_Approx 528 for P-185 counts AD and NC auxiliary subjects; the conversion analysis uses 221 MCI.
The registry Modality 'MRI/PET' is wrong for both (T1 sMRI; DTI).
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in P-152 as published: it would take a pMCI-vs-sMCI result from P-152, which the paper does not contain.
